title: Rust GUI migration hierarchy: entrypoints, editors and expected controls
scope: Main-menu entrypoints, all exported native Slint windows, popup/importer surfaces and source-backed nested editor/control families. Missing expected controls are anchored at implementation omissions or placeholders.
caveats: Historical audit provenance is source inspection. Reviewed implementation changes passed hosted CI; per-node remaining boundaries still apply.
All 121 exported Slint Window components have assessed nested controls or canonical shared-editor navigation.
Statuses describe identified slices. Existing recordings/assertion bodies are cited precisely where inspected; callback presence alone does not establish a first pass.
Missing controls may anchor a parent implementation or placeholder boundary, with explicit omission evidence; such anchors do not imply a native control exists.
Contextual disabled states, absent dynamic data and informational labels are distinguished from no-op actions and explicit missing functionality.
Shared editors and inferred open-call relationships describe finite navigation; aliases are not separate implementations.

The map selects meaningful controls/workflows rather than every widget or runtime state. Remote administration, richer maintenance, importer, predicate and formula workflows have concrete missing entries.
Reference and native inventories have different granularity; their node/status/navigation counts are not an overall feature denominator or parity percentage.

status_definitions.first_pass: Identified native slice with reference-backed regression evidence; broader parity not asserted.
status_definitions.partial: Implemented native slice with documented omissions, family limitations or explicitly unverified behavioral boundaries.
status_definitions.missing: Explicit placeholder or documented unsupported native editing/action slice.
status_definitions.unassessed: Surface exists, but behavioral completion was not assessed.

nodes.label: Hydrus Rust native GUI

evidence.description: Native desktop behavior and feature-specific integration descriptions; used as context alongside the inspected control/callback paths.
Remaining network, tag/archive and downloader-definition breadth priorities.

remaining_limitations: Remote repository/IPFS/account administration and login-editor execution remain deferred.
Tag archive/hash-conversion migration, unsupported formula-kind GUI editors and database maintenance dialogs have explicit missing branches.
Supported media/import/service workflows retain narrower source-backed control limitations in their descendants.
nodes.assessment: The map traces the native main menus, all known native Window components, non-window controls and their nested shared editors against the reference panels. Implemented local-store/media/import/Client API workflows coexist with explicit missing repository/admin, login, database-maintenance and editor controls. Child assessments identify each supported slice and its gaps; this organizational root summarizes mixed coverage and does not certify whole-client parity.

nodes.label: Search predicate undo history

native_source.description: Inspected this native subsystem and its callbacks; Reference keeps added/removed predicate batches and builds addition/removal submenus; native SearchPage enters/removes predicates without a matching undo-history model.

nodes.assessment: Frame-owned, transient, separate deduplicated addition/removal recency lists populate the actual searching submenus newest first. Typed stable commands toggle the selected historical predicate on the currently visible media page, retire its entry before recording the resulting delta, and leave stale commands inert. New/restored page predicates do not enter history; histories survive page close/restore, apply across pages and stay independent across windows. Committed typed OR is one entry; cancelled predicate children and refused inputs add none. Undo enters a locked page hidden query while retaining its lock; with an empty notebook selected, it preserves history. Clear history uses the exact reference confirmation: rejection retains both lists; acceptance clears both without changing searches or closed-page history. History names use raw predicate text despite hidden-namespace presentation. Populated locked pages retain their prior lock badge and media even with synchronization enabled; locking and hash synchronization update the cached panel count. Accepted system values preserve originating Shift intent: drafts extend without frame history; normal activation merges into one committed OR history entry. Accepting a system value and later cancelling its outer OR leaves frame history unchanged while retaining actual reference recent predicates.

evidence.description: Inspected this native subsystem and its callbacks; Reference keeps added/removed predicate batches and builds addition/removal submenus; native SearchPage enters/removes predicates without a matching undo-history model.
